specification_compliance: r8 CR8-1 is fixed. Commit fcb2c95 moves the submodule to 7b233ee, which removes `import contextlib`, `import time` and `Iterator` from file_question.py. A grep of the worktree finds no remaining use of `contextlib`, `time.` or `Iterator`. The imports still present (`asyncio`, `threading`, `Mapping`, `Sequence`, `replace`, `PYMUPDF_LOCK`) are all used: threading.Event at :769, Mapping at :712 and :1367, replace at :1442, PYMUPDF_LOCK at :1040 and :1063.

I8 is unchanged from r8. PageImages.open() (file_question.py:1037-1045) acquires PYMUPDF_LOCK once, waiting at most 30 s, and then opens the document. image() renders through _render_page, whose Page and Pixmap locals are freed under the hold. close() (:1054-1063) closes the document and drops it before releasing the lock in its finally block.

I1-I7 and I9: this round changes no product logic. The diff of the full change matches my reading in earlier rounds: uses_document_tools and the branch order, the 3-call cap and the final request with tool_choice none, whole-row text walks with the reserve counted, numbering of passages before pages, the meta image states, a fallback through today's text request with no requested material, the page rules in spec order, and logs that carry only class names, counts and the file id.
r8 CR8-2 (no test that the Document is deallocated under the lock) is not addressed in this round. It stays a test gap, and the code still holds the property.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A page request holds PYMUPDF_LOCK from opening the PDF until up to 4 pages are rendered and the document is closed, so an extraction that starts during that time waits for the whole request.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: If someone asks about PDF pages while another PDF is being indexed, the indexing waits a few extra seconds, and the user notices nothing.

regression_risks: The import removal has no runtime effect. If some code outside file_question.py imported `time`, `contextlib` or `Iterator` through this module, it would now fail. I found no such re-export use in the files I read, but I did not search the whole addon.
test_coverage: This round changes no tests. The tests' coverage is as in r8: strong acceptance tests for the walk, the limits, numbering, the fallbacks, the deadline, keep-alive, the log line, no writes, and lock-held freeing of Page and Pixmap.
There is still no test of Document deallocation under the lock (r8 CR8-2), of the final-request keep-alive after a whitespace-only first delta (r6 CR-4), or of absolute NFD paths (r6 CR-3).
